newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to Europe air cargo rates rise twice in 10 days.
newsitem.headline: HK to Europe air cargo rates rise twice in 10 days.

text.p: There is to be a second rise in 10 days in air cargo rates from Hong Kong to Europe, industry sources told Reuters.

Freight forwarders said they have already been sent warning notices about the HK$2 a kg rise from October 10. Rates were raised at the start of the month by HK$2 a kg. This followed a HK$3 a kg increase at the beginning of August by airlines complaining of low rates and yields.

They blamed the latest rise on higher operating costs and increased jet fuel prices in Asia. The average per kg rate will be around HK$25 a kg from October 10, compared to just over HK HK$21 at end-September.

"I was a little bit reluctant to agree a rise because twice in 10 days is a little bit much but we will try and see how the market reacts. If we have to come back and reduce it within two or three weeks, then we will do it," said the regional cargo manager for Air France Cargo, Philippe Bour.
Industry sources said the airlines are taking advantage of a strong market where supply is unable to meet demand for European destinations.

"Quite a lot of agents are complaining but I think the market can stand another rise because customers are struggling to get space," Hong Kong cargo manager for Dubai-based Emirates Air Services, Jacky Lau said.
But Anthony Lau, vice-chairmanman of the Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents is alarmed by the latest increase.

"I think it is disturbing. I can understand the market is very firm and we are still below what we used to pay six or seven years ago but the timing and the way it has been handled leaves room for improvement," he said.

"Customers will have to accept it because we are in the middle of the peak season and if the market continues to be firm the new rate will hold," Lau added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
